newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gasoline prices seen steady through summer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gasoline prices seen steady through summer.

text.p: Gasoline prices should hold at relatively low levels through the summer and ease slightly through the end of the year if underlying oil markets remain calm, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Tuesday.
But prices should rebound by about 5 cents per gallon next spring as the new driving season begins, the Energy Department's statistical and forecasting agency said.
Retail gasoline prices for this year appeared to have peaked in January at an average $1.32 per gallon, and eased an average 7 cents per gallon by last month, the EIA said.
It projected prices to stay fairly low through this summer driving season that ends Labor Day weekend.

The EIA also examined the gasoline price spikes during spring last year that prompted an outcry by a number of congressmen and complaints that refiners were keeping inventories too tight and exacerbating price rises.
But the EIA said the prices spikes were "explained largely by markets in crude oil and normal seasonal behavior."
The winter of 1997 then was warmer than usual and new crude supplies arrived from Iraq and other sources, bringing prices down for crude oil and gasoline, it said.

"Retail gasoline prices declined 6 cents per gallon from January through May. As a result of the lower crude oil prices, EIA expects gasoline prices to remain below those of last year during the remainder of the summer driving season," the agency said.
